Intraoperative precursor events refer to any factors or conditions that occur during a surgical procedure before it is completed. These can include various risks, complications, or uncertainties that may affect the outcome of the surgery. Major adverse events (MAEs) are severe and life-threatening complications that can arise from these intraoperative precursor events.

Research has shown that patients who experience intraoperative precursor events are at a higher risk of experiencing major adverse events post-operatively. This is because some of these events, such as those related to cardiopulmonary bypass or anesthesia, can be directly or indirectly linked to the underlying conditions or risks identified in the intraoperative period.

Studies have found associations between certain intraoperative precursor events and increased rates of postoperative major adverse events. For example, patients who undergo cardiac surgery exposed to intraoperative precursor events may be more likely to experience a postoperative major adverse cardiovascular event (MACE). Similarly, patients undergoing open TME (transformer receptor-positive muscle esophageal cancer metastasis) with intraoperative neuromonitoring may have lower rates of urinary and anorectal dysfunction if they are experiencing profound hypotensive events.

While the exact mechanisms by which intraoperative precursor events lead to major adverse events remain unclear, it is essential to mitigate these risks through quality improvement techniques. This can involve strategies such as:

* Enhanced preoperative evaluation and risk assessment for patients undergoing cardiac surgery
* Optimizing anesthesia and perioperative care protocols to reduce hypotension and other complications
* Implementing robust postoperative monitoring and follow-up care to identify and address potential issues early

By understanding the associations between intraoperative precursor events and major adverse events, we can work towards improving surgical outcomes for patients undergoing various types of procedures.
